##### Feature idea summary
Make sure `memory mode = dbengine` is the default. For that to be the case we need to finish:
- Stress testing
- Instrumentation & Characterization
- Benchmarking

Tasks:
- [x] Combine and parallelize dbengine validation unittest with dataset generator into a multithreaded dbengine benchmark that validates data integrity while constantly generating new data.
- [ ] Run k6 load generator and get API performance numbers.
- [ ] Combine k6 load testing with dbengine dataset generation to get API query performance numbers with heavy data collection interference.
- [x] List the OSs where we know it is supported OOB
    - See whether `kickstart.sh` enables `dbengine` on OSs without manually installing repositories below:
    - [x] Ubuntu 18.04
    - [ ] CentOS 6
    - [ ] CentOS 7
    - [ ] Debian 8
    - [x] Debian 9
    - [x] Debian 10
    - [ ] Manjaro 18
    - [x] Fedora 30
    - [x] openSUSE 15
    - [ ] FreeBSD 12 (not supported by `kickstart.sh`)
- [x] Make the default memory mode `dbengine` when the support is compiled in the netdata binary

review_comments: `unsigned` type for the majority of the compilers is `unsigned integer`, but the function ``` strtoul``` returns `unsigned long' that is bigger than `unsigned` for 64 bits host, so I think it is better to keep the cast here.
```random()``` returns `long int`, to avoid warnings, I think it is good to cast here.
I haven't seen any warnings from the compiler or static analysis. Until we see an actual warning I think we shouldn't pollute the code with unnecessary casts.
I will compile this PR in a 32 bits computer to confirm that the warning is not present.
I tested in 32 bits computer and I also compiled with clang, there was not any warning for both compilation.
why are you not using ```error()``` function here?
The binary is running as standalone, there is no service running or logging being set-up. It's running like this `./netdata -W stresstest=10`
